pr_title: sql: Add a SHOW NODES command
pr_body:
This PR adds a SHOW NODES command that displays the same data as the
cockroach node status command.

Fixes #40445.

Release note (sql change): Adds a SHOW NODES command that displays the
same data as cockroach node status.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/40636)
Tests added. I'll wait for discussion about the choice of table to query before looking to merge however.

Thanks Andrei for your comment.

Rohan I don't know (I really *don't know*) whether to move forward on this *now* -- I think it's dangerous to bake a user-facing feature, and then start advertising it in docs, if we have even a moderate expectation that it will show confusing data that can increase our support burden.

FWIW the list of nodes in the admin UI uses a different source for the data, and that is the list that users use most often (I think that the CLI `cockroach node status` is less used overall). 

It may well be that the proper way forward would be to make the "node status map" (which merges the data from both gossip and KV together) used by the UI and a few other RPCs also available in SQL, and then have both `cockroach node status` and `SHOW NODES` query that. (There's a caveat that we may want `cockroach node status` , which is also a troubleshooting tool, to report partial results even when the status range is unavailable and the KV query would hang, so the code in there—but not in SHOW NODES or the UI—may need a 2-pronged approach).

Perhaps it's also possible to get this data by using a SQL join between `gossip_nodes`, `gossip_liveness` and `kv_node_status`, but that may be more complex and I am not 100% sure it would be equivalent (that needs to be investigated).

In any case I really think it's desirable to invest into making all the various channels use a common source of truth instead of doubling down on the dubious approach used by `cockroach node status`. 

Bottom line:

1) keep the PR open until we figure out how to improve both this new feature and also `cockroach node status`.  

2) recognize/acknowledge that we are "opening the blackbox" of `crdb_internal` (see https://github.com/cockroachdb/docs/pull/4326) so we can explain to users the difference between `gossip_nodes` and  `kv_node_status`  so they can decide themselves what they want, until we provide something better.
@rohany FYI for an example of a real bug that existed before because code was erroneously using only gossip instead of gossip+KV, see #26821.
Tagging @tbg to help us think over this when you're back from vacay.
Thanks for the detailed comments @knz. We can keep this on the backburner until we have a better idea of what to do.
Devils advocate: could we move forward here with the same logic as the cockroach node status and then come back and update both at the same time?

I'm +1 on merging as is. If `cockroach node status` already shows this same information, then we're not doing worse than before - we're merely consistently broadcasting what another command knows to be true. If this is problematic, we will find out, and solve it in the next release.

I'd question if we need this statement in the first place. Can't we muddle along with the virtual tables and the cli command for longer? I'd take a predisposition for inaction when it comes to adding new sql commands. I question whether nodes are even a fundamental cockroach concept that warrants such language integration; in Cockroach Cloud for example we should be moving away from talking about nodes. And even if they are, I'd take time to debate the columns returned by this command. I wonder about the updated_at column, which suggests a surprising execution model for this command (presenting some sort of historical info instead of "up to date" info), and I don't really know what live and available mean (they're not properly documented for the cli command).
What permissions/grants would a user need to be allowed to perform this command?

> f cockroach node status already shows this same information, then we're not doing worse than before - we're merely consistently broadcasting what another command knows to be true.

Counterpoint:

If `cockroach node status` is currently wrong, we have to fix it.
If we introduce a new `SHOW NODES` on top of this and it's also wrong, no we have two things to fix and test instead of just one.

I'm not keen on doubling down on tech debt just because we're ok with debt in general. Interest accrues unpleasingly.
